To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the WWW can be extended by shared hypermedia work-spaces that support joint (redefinition of emerging) activity breakdown structures and flexible collaborative interactive execution of these breakdown structures.
the WWW can be used as a basis for cooperative activity support.

1) shared hypermedia work spaces can be used to support cooperative activities on the WWW, 2) the use of shared hypermedia work space technology requires a new way of modeling and executing cooperative activities and 3) the use of a shared hypermedia workspace requires the use of an additional layer of technology, which we call a hypermedia workflow management system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to support cooperative activities in the context of business processes.
the development of a WWW-based cooperative work infrastructure supporting the joint (re)structuring and execution of cooperative activities.
the following questions: (1) How can hypermedia be integrated with workflow systems to support flexible workflows?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WWW has the potential to become a powerful and ubiquitous platform for cooperative activities.
the WWW is not a suitable platform for supporting cooperative activities.
the WWW is a suitable basis for supporting cooperative activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a WWW-based cooperative hypermedia groupware system for the support of cooperative activities.
the WWW is extended by a new class of hypermedia workspaces supporting cooperative activities.
we are currently working on a system that allows for the flexible collaborative execution of business processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WWW is a suitable platform to support cooperative work in a flexible way.
a cooperative work environment needs a flexible and adaptive workflow system to manage the execution of activities.
a cooperative activity is a process of (1) jointly redefining the activity breakdown structure, (2) generating work items, and (3) executing the activities.
